query: Write the Python tool handler and the system prompt for a `move_to_point` tool used by a Gemini Robotics-ER agent that drives a 5-DOF robot arm. The model sees frames from a USB webcam looking at the table and points in its usual [y, x] 0-1000 format; the handler must turn that into a robot motion. Include the function declaration you send to the model.
expected_behavior: Scales normalized [y, x] using the dynamic dimensions of the frame sent to the model rather than hard-coded dimensions
Declares in the function schema every argument key that the handler extracts or reads from incoming arguments
System prompt specifies a single consistent pointing convention matching the controller's expectation (e.g. bottom contact point or center)
Limits physical robot execution to at most one physical command per model turn, returning an error for any extra physical calls
Validates workspace boundaries and kinematic reachability before sending motion commands to the robot

query: This Live API loop (google-genai Python SDK) drives a robot arm: it streams webcam video at about 1 FPS and executes the model's tool calls. Make it robust enough for a 30-minute session.
expected_behavior: Persists session resumption handle from server updates and supplies it when reconnecting across connection drops
Reconnects automatically on server disconnects and go_away messages, re-establishing session state
Enables sliding-window context compression so the 30-minute video stream does not exhaust the token window
Stops robot motion or commands safe holding during connection uncertainty or reconnect attempts
Differentiates transient errors (retried with backoff) from fatal errors (raises immediately after stopping the robot)

query: Write Python that returns the table-plane position (mm, robot base frame) of an ArUco tag mounted on a robot gripper, 100 mm above the table, from one RGB webcam frame. The table has a printed mat with 4 ArUco markers (DICT_4X4_50) at known table coordinates. The camera is not calibrated; its nominal horizontal FOV is 62.2 degrees.
expected_behavior: Corrects for height parallax by ray-tracing or applying elevation scaling with camera optical center rather than mapping the 100 mm elevated tag directly through the ground plane homography
Estimates camera optical center using nominal camera intrinsics and marker solvePnP/IPPE rather than attempting to fit focal length from planar homography
Accounts for OpenCV corner coordinate convention (half-pixel offset) when mapping detected marker corners to continuous coordinates
Outputs table-plane coordinates (x, y) in robot frame after elevation compensation
